([[Jersey City, New Jersey]]) | college = * [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky]] (2016–2018) * [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]] (2018–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team1 = [[Maine Celtics]] | highlights = * [[MAAC men's basketball tournament|MAAC tournament]] MVP ([[2021 MAAC men's basketball tournament|2021]]) * [[Ohio Valley Conference|OVC]] All-Newcomer Team (2017) }} '''Asante Jamar Gist''' (born January 20, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky Colonels]] and the [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona Gaels]]. ==High school career== Raised in [[East Orange, New Jersey]],Zagoria, Adam. [https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2020/03/former-nj-high-school-star-hoping-to-make-history-with-rick-pitino-at-iona.html "Former N.J. high school star hoping to make history with Rick Pitino at Iona"], NJ Advance Media for [[NJ.com]], March 22, 2020. Accessed December 18, 2024. "After speaking to the Eastern Kentucky players, Pitino pulled East Orange native Asante Gist aside for a one-on-one chat." Gist began his high school career at [[Roselle Catholic High School]] and won the NJSIAA Tournament of Champions as a freshman. For his junior season, he transferred to [[Marist High School (New Jersey)|Marist High School]] due to the emergence of [[Isaiah Briscoe]].{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Eastern Kentucky-Bound Asante Gist Leads St. Anthony’s Over St. Patrick’s in Rivalry Game |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2016/01/17/eastern-kentucky-bound-asante-gist-leads-st-anthonys-over-st-patricks-in-rivalry-game/ |website=ZagsBlog |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=January 17, 2016}} Gist averaged 14.8 points per game in 13 games. He transferred to [[St. Anthony High School (New Jersey)|St. Anthony High School]] for his senior season.{{cite news |last1=Schneider |first1=Jeremy |title=Boys Basketball: Marist guard Asante Gist transfers to St. Anthony |url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/article/boys-basketball-marist-guard-asante-gist-transfers-to-st-anthony/ |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=August 24, 2019}} Gist helped lead the Friars to a 32–0 record and a victory in the Tournament of Champions. He scored 16 points in the title game against [[Linden High School (New Jersey)|Linden High School]].{{cite news |last1=Canova |first1=Dan |title=Former St. Anthony hoops star transfers to Iona |url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2018/01/former_st_anthony_standout_gist_transfers_to_iona.html |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=January 18, 2018}} In November 2015, Gist committed to playing college basketball for [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky]] over offers from [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] and [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]] in large part because of the recruiting pitch of coach [[Dan McHale]]. ==College career== As a freshman, Gist averaged 15.9 points and 3.8 assists per game. He suffered from a right ankle injury and played in six games as a sophomore, averaging eight points and 2.7 assists per game. On January 18, 2018, Gist transferred to [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]] and received a waiver from the NCAA for eligibility in December.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Iona lands Eastern Kentucky transfer Asante Gist |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/01/18/iona-lands-eastern-kentucky-transfer-asante-gist/ |website=ZagsBlog |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=January 18, 2018}} As a junior, he averaged 12.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Welser |first1=Joel |title=#95 IONA MEN'S BASKETBALL 2019-2020 PREVIEW |url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/17670 |website=College Sports Madness |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=August 3, 2019}} Gist appeared in 15 games as a redshirt junior before missing the rest of the season with an injury. He averaged 10.1 points, 2.2 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game.{{cite news |title=Towson vs. Iona odds, line: 2020 college basketball picks, Dec. 29 predictions from proven model |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/towson-vs-iona-odds-line-2020-college-basketball-picks-dec-29-predictions-from-proven-model/ |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 29, 2020}} Gist was limited by surgery on his finger and a debilitating back injury during his senior season.{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=March Madness 2021: Iona’s Asante Gist, N.J. native, eyes NCAA Tournament upset of Alabama to cap medical comeback |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2021/03/march-madness-2021-ionas-asante-gist-nj-native-eyes-ncaa-tournament-upset-of-alabama-to-cap-medical-comeback.html |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=March 19, 2021}} He helped Iona win the [[2021 MAAC men's basketball tournament|2021 MAAC tournament]], earning MVP honors after scoring 18 points in the title game against [[Fairfield Stags men's basketball|Fairfield]], and reach the NCAA Tournament.{{cite web |title=Iona Wins the 2021 MAAC Men’s Basketball Championship |url=https://maacsports.com/news/2021/3/13/iona-wins-the-2021-maac-mens-basketball-championship.aspx |website=[[Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference]] |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=March 13, 2021}} Gist averaged 13.4 points and 3.6 assists per game.{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Brooklyn Nets sign ex-Patrick School star DeAndre’ Bembry; Former Roselle Catholic, St. Anthony’s standout Asante Gist to play Summer League with Wizards |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2021/08/brooklyn-nets-sign-ex-patrick-school-star-deandre-bembry-former-roselle-catholic-st-anthonys-standout-asante-gist-to-play-summer-league-with-wizards.html |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=August 8, 2021}} He was named to the Second Team All-Met by the Met Basketball Writers Association.{{cite news |last1=Rapay |first1=Eugene |title=Iona's Ross, Gist, Seton Hall's Espinoza-Hunter highlight Division I All-Met awards |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/college/2021/04/27/all-met-team-iona-ross-gist-seton-hall-espinoza-hunter/4852625001/ |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[The Journal News]] |date=April 27, 2021}} ==Professional career== Gist played for the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2021 NBA Summer League]] and was selected in the third round of the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite news |title=Asante Gist: Will play for Westchester |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/asante-gist-will-play-for-westchester/ |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 25, 2021}} He was waived on December 2, 2021, before appearing in a game.{{cite news |title=Asante Gist: Cut loose by Westchester |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/asante-gist-cut-loose-by-westchester/ |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=December 2, 2021}} On December 17, Gist was acquired by the [[Maine Celtics]] and scored 11 points in his debut in a 111–99 win against the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite news |last1=Eid |first1=David |title=Maine Celtics top the Long Island Nets 111-99 |url=https://wgme.com/sports/content/maine-celtics-top-the-long-island-nets-111-99 |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=WGME |date=December 17, 2021}} He was waived on February 1, 2022. Gist was re-acquired by the team on February 21.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|access-date=February 24, 2022}} Gist was then later waived on February 28, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 28,
